BILL NUMBER:  S250

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend chapter 50 of the laws of 2008, enacting the public
protection and general government budget; to amend chapter 53 of the
laws of 2008, enacting the education, labor and family assistance
budget; to amend chapter 54 of the laws of 2008, enacting the health
and mental hygiene budget; and to amend chapter 55 of the laws of
2008, enacting the transportation, economic development and
environmental conservation budget, in relation to the support of state
government


 PURPOSE :
This bill would amend the enacted 2008-09 Budget appropriation bills,
as amended this past August, to effect savings proposed by the
Governor to address the multi-year Financial Plan gap and respond to
the worsening national economic conditions faced by the State. Other
bills being proposed in concert with this legislation would make
non-appropriation statutory changes needed to implement the proposed
savings.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Effective immediately upon enactment, this bill makes the following
changes to appropriations highlighted as follows:

* Reduces appropriations for Local Government Efficiency Grants and
Efficiency Incentive Grants by amounts that will honor existing grant
awards in full, but reduce funding for new grants by 50 percent and
limit Local Government Efficiency Grant administrative expenses to
$500,000, generating savings of $1.7 million in 2008-09 and $13.6
million in 2009-10;

* Reduces 2008-09 funding for arts grants by $7 million;

* Increases 2008-09 General Fund support by $12 million to accommodate
greater Tuition Assistance Program (TAP) spending that will result
from State University of New York (SUNY) tuition rate increases;

* Increases 2008-09 tuition revenue offset appropriations for SUNY by
$76 million and reduces General Fund support for SUNY by $68 million,
reflecting resident tuition rate increases of 14 percent;

* Reduces 2008-09 General Fund support by $11 million for SUNY
Community College base operating aid and $4 million for CUNY Community
College base operating aid;

* Achieves over $70 million in savings in Medicaid and certain other
Health programs and offsetting HCRA revenues (other statutory changes
needed to produce this savings are proposed in a separate bill);

* Achieves $1 million in 2008-09 savings by delaying implementation of
slots for the foster care Bridges to Health Medicaid Waiver program
until 2011-12;

* Reduces appropriations for Mental Hygiene-related purposes by
eliminating enriched Unified Services funding for certain counties and
lowering funding to the NYC Department of Education for prevention
services that are not predicated upon evidence-based practices;

* Reduces 2008-09 funding for new and enhanced legislative programs by
a cumulative total of 50 percent in 2008-09 and 2009-10;

* Reduces the 2008-09 Human Services Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA)
by one percentage point for certain programs administered by the
Department of Health, Office of Alcoholism and Substance Abuse
Services, Office of Children and Family Services, Office of Mental
Health, Office of Mental Retardation and Developmental Disabilities,
and State Office for the Aging;

* Reduces 2008-09 General Fund Local Assistance for various economic
development initiatives by $8.5 million;

* Reduces 2008-09 Environmental Protection Fund appropriations by $50
million in various categories relating to Open Space, Solid Waste and
Parks and Recreation;

* Achieves $2 million in 2008-09 savings by reducing appropriations
for the Neighborhood Preservation Program and the Rural Preservation
Program;

* Achieves $3 million in 2008-09 savings by eliminating the operating
subsidy for the New York City Housing Authority;

* Achieves $25 million in 2008-09 Financial Plan relief by creating
three new bonded capital appropriations for affordable housing
programs that were previously supported on a pay-as-you-go basis;

* Shifts the funding for Timothy's Law and various Department of
Health programs from the General Fund to the Insurance Department's
industry assessment;

* Achieves $3 million in 2008-09 savings by eliminating a one-time
appropriation from 2007-08 for diesel emissions reduction costs; and

* Achieves $1.1 million in 2008-09 savings by eliminating a one-time
2008-09 appropriation for multi-modal projects;

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :
The Financial Plan savings resulting from this bill are part of the
package of savings options proposed to help close the gap and to help
ensure that the current year's budget remains in balance if economic
conditions deteriorate further.

 BUDGETARY IMPLICATIONS :
In combination with other legislation that proposes statutory changes
and fund transfers, this bill would produce the savings noted above.
These savings would substantially reduce the current 2008-09 and
2009-10 projected and beyond.

summary: Makes amendments to certain appropriations made by chapters 50, 53, 54 and 55 of the laws of 2008 relating to support of state government to effect savings to address the multi-year financial plan gap.
